_comment: The Grade 3 Computing standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Fourteen lessons organised by the strands of Cambridge Primary Computing 0059 Stage 3 (36 objectives), NOT by the units of the Word-pack course under computing/grade-3/data, so progress is written under l01..l14 - see THE UNIT PROBLEM in wire-progress.py. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall.
subject: computing
hubStrands: Following, editing and correcting linear algorithms; why an efficient algorithm is concise; the steps that repeat inside everyday tasks; logical thinking; predicting what a change will do; dividing a task into smaller sections; the inputs to an algorithm, and algorithms that turn an input into an output.

Editing programs to be clear and concise; resetting objects at the start; more than one algorithm running at the same time; programs with more than one object, one of them static; changing a number inside a block; an output from an input device; working with others; learning from mistakes; testing and debugging; programming a physical device.

Problems that data can solve; different ways of representing data with a digital tool; recording discrete and categorical data; spreadsheets of rows, columns and cells; formatting cells for their purpose; selecting data by its characteristics.

Networked hardware at school and at home; the services a network offers - files, printing, the World Wide Web; the advantages and disadvantages of a network; ciphers that keep information secret, and a code where 1 is a, 2 is b.

Hardware and software combining into a working system, and their different roles; manual and automatic input devices; the kinds of file a computer stores; computers that control machines; Internet of Things devices at home; robots in manufacturing.
